name: Arvid Lunnemark

education.notes: Met his three Cursor co-founders (Michael Truell, Sualeh Asif, Aman Sanger) while studying CS and mathematics at MIT.

keyDecisions: Co-founded Anysphere / Cursor in 2022 while at MIT with three classmates — student-cohort founding pattern.
Built an AI-native code editor at the exact moment large language models became viable for code generation.
Scaled to $29.3B valuation and $2B+ ARR by early 2026 — one of the fastest software company growth arcs ever recorded.
Departed Cursor in October 2025 to start Integrous Research — a safety-focused AI research lab.
lessons: MIT CS classmate cohort is one of the few founding-team structures with both technical depth and pre-existing trust.
Founding at 21 in the AI revolution is viable only if you and your co-founders are at the technical frontier — not as a general template.
Stepping away from a $29B company at 25 to start a safety lab is a credible second-act when the first venture was a generational outcome.
Swedish-origin founders can compete at the frontier from the US — but the path requires elite-US-CS-cohort access (MIT), not just talent.
careerSteps.notes: Cursor / Anysphere founded 2022 at MIT. Scaled to $29.3B valuation and $2B+ ARR by early 2026 per Forbes / Inc / The Information. Lunnemark left in October 2025 to found Integrous Research.

keyDecisions: Founded Integrous Research in October 2025 — a safety-focused AI research lab.
Chose research / alignment over operating a $29B company — explicit values-driven second act.
lessons: Second-act founders post-mega-outcome can credibly start research labs — the rare exit-path when the first venture is a $1B+ outcome.
Values-driven pivots (safety / alignment) are becoming a credible second-venture pattern among AI billionaires under 30.

Cursor's MIT classmate cohort (Truell, Asif, Sanger, Lunnemark) is the modern version of the Stanford-PayPal-mafia pattern — pre-existing trust + technical depth + frontier timing.
